subs.text: Book one.
Athena Inspires the Prince.
Scene one.
The Gods Consider Odysseus.
The gods take their places in a widening ring.
Poseidon’s seat remains empty.
How mortals love to blame the gods for their sorrows.
Think of Aegisthus, who took Agamemnon's wife and cut the king down at his homecoming,
though we sent Hermes himself to warn him.
His own recklessness doubled the fate he was owed.
Father Zeus, let Aegisthus lie in the ruin he earned.
It is Odysseus my heart breaks for, wise, unlucky Odysseus, held against his will on Calypso's island,
longing only for the sight of smoke rising from his own hearth.
Has he not paid you sacrifice enough on the plain of Troy, Olympian?
My child, how could I forget godlike Odysseus?
It is Poseidon the earth-shaker who rages without rest for the blinding of his Cyclops son,
and drives that man from his homecoming.
But come, let us here shape his return;
one god cannot hold out against us all.

scenes.title: Athena's Two-Part Plan
scenes.card: Athena plans to free Odysseus from the island where a goddess holds him, and to go herself to wake up his son.

subs.text: Scene two.
Athena's Two-Part Plan.
Then send Hermes, the guide, the slayer of Argus, across the water to Ogygia at once.
Let him stand before the nymph Calypso with our fixed decree:
hard-enduring Odysseus goes home.
And I go to Ithaca myself, to breathe strength into his son.
I will set Telemachus on his feet, send him to call the Achaeans to assembly,
and then across the sea to Pylos and Sparta for news of his father, so the boy may win a name among men.
So the gods divided the labor:
release the father, waken the son.
Two roads laid down at once, bending toward a single homecoming.
Athena fastens the gold sandals, closes her hand around the spear, and drops from Olympus.

scenes.title: The Stranger at the Threshold
scenes.card: Disguised as a traveling stranger, Athena arrives at Odysseus's house, where the suitors are feasting, and Telemachus welcomes her in.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Stranger at the Threshold.
Wearing the shape of Mentes, Athena waits at the palace threshold with her spear upright.
Dice strike the floor;
cups are filled;
the suitors never look toward the gate.
Telemachus sees the unattended stranger and crosses the hall, ashamed of his own house.
Welcome, stranger.
You are kindly come to our house;
give me your spear.
Eat first, and afterward tell me what you need, but come, away from this noise.

scenes.title: Mentes Questions the Prince
scenes.card: Telemachus complains that the suitors are eating up his missing father's wealth; the disguised goddess tells him his father is alive.

subs.text: Scene four.
Mentes Questions the Prince.
Telemachus gives the stranger the chair of honor and sits close enough to keep the conversation private.
You see them, stranger.
They devour another man's substance without payment, a man whose white bones lie rotting in the rain somewhere,
or rolling in the salt surf.
If he had fallen at Troy I could bear it;
instead these men eat my house to nothing, and soon enough they will tear me apart as well.
I am Mentes, son of wise Anchialus, lord of the oar-loving Taphians, and your father's guest-friend of old;
ask grizzled Laertes if you doubt it.
And hear this from me:
Odysseus is not dead.
He is held on a sea-girt island by rough men, and he will contrive his way home,
for no man alive is richer in devices.
But tell me truly, are you Odysseus's own son?
Your head, your fine eyes, you are marvelously like him as I knew him.
And what is this feast, this mob filling the house?
A wedding?
For no man of sense could stomach such insolence under his own roof.

scenes.title: Athena Arms Telemachus with a Course
scenes.card: Athena tells Telemachus to stand up to the suitors in public and to sail away in search of news of his father.

subs.text: Scene five.
Athena Arms Telemachus with a Course.
My mother neither refuses a marriage she hates nor makes an end of the matter.
So from Dulichium and Same and wooded Zacynthus, and from rocky Ithaca itself, they come courting her,
and day by day they grind my house to nothing.
Shame on them all.
Oh, for Odysseus at that doorway now, helmet and shield and his two spears,
the man I first knew in our house drinking and glad.
A bitter, brief wooing they would find;
their deaths would come down on every one of them like night.
Now hear me, and do it.
Tomorrow call the Achaean lords to assembly and bid the suitors scatter, each man to his own home.
Then fit out a ship of twenty oars and go for news of your long-gone father, to Nestor at Pylos first,
then to sandy Sparta and red-haired Menelaus, the last of the bronze-clad Achaeans home.
Have you not heard what fame Orestes won among men, striking down the schemer who murdered his famous father?
You are tall and well-made, my friend;
be brave, so that men born after you will speak your name.
Childish things are done now;
put them from you.

scenes.title: The Goddess Departs; the Prince Speaks
scenes.card: The goddess flies off like a bird; Telemachus, newly bold, sends his grieving mother upstairs and calls a public meeting for dawn.

subs.text: Scene six.
The Goddess Departs;
the Prince Speaks.
Do not hold me longer, my road calls.
Whatever gift your heart bids you give, keep it for my homeward passing, and it will be repaid with its equal.
The goddess rises like a bird;
Telemachus returns to the hall with his posture changed.
Phemius, break off this bitter song, it wastes my heart in my breast.
You know many another;
sing the deeds of men and gods, but not the Achaeans' coming home.
Mother, let the singer sing as his mind moves him;
Odysseus is not the only man who never came home from Troy.
Go up to your rooms and tend your own work, the loom and the distaff;
speech will be the concern of men, and mine above all, for the authority in this house is mine.
And at dawn I call the assembly.
Night sealed the household, but Telemachus lay awake inside the course Athena had set.

prologue: A king named Odysseus left his island of Ithaca to fight a ten-year war at Troy, and ten more years have passed without his return. At home his wife and son wait while a crowd of local men eat his food and press his wife to marry one of them and take his throne. Now the gods decide to bring him home.
